identity.name: Lateral Tool Transfer + Chisel Tunnel + PsExec Fan-Out (Muddled Libra Playbook) — First T1570 ABIOC (SIM-EDR-015)
identity.summary: An endpoint pulls an archive over HTTPS, writes and executes a never-before-seen tunneler (chisel), opens a long-lived TCP/443 tunnel, then fans out PsExec/RDP to internal peers — the Muddled Libra lateral-tool-transfer playbook. The ABIOC fires on the transfer-and-fan-out deviation from the host baseline, anchored to the download -> first-seen-tool -> peer-connection causality chain.
identity.description: First-party Cortex ABIOC coverage for MITRE T1570 (Lateral Tool Transfer) on the endpoint plane, modeling the operational playbook Unit 42 attributes to Muddled Libra / Scattered Spider (UNC3944). After obtaining valid local-administrator credentials on a rogue VM, the operator downloads 'goon.zip' from an attacker-controlled AWS S3 bucket, extracts and executes chisel.exe to stand up a persistent (~15h) SSH tunnel over TCP/443, creates a local 'gooner' account for interactive access, then fans out with PsExec and RDP against internal peers before offline NTDS.dit theft from powered-down domain controllers. Every tool used (chisel, PsExec, S3 Browser, ADRecon) is a legitimate admin/dual-use utility — the adversary deliberately prefers legitimate tools and existing infrastructure to blend in, so a hand-authored BIOC keyed on a specific bad hash or command string is brittle. This card exercises the Analytics Behavioral IOC (ABIOC) detector class — PANW-authored, auto-tuned behavioral-ML anchored to a learned causality chain — against that tradecraft. Two ABIOCs cover the two deviation shapes: (1) an HTTPS-fetched archive whose downloader process is the direct causality parent of a never-before-seen tunneler/remote-exec binary (the lateral-tool-transfer signal), and (2) that newly-written tool fanning out remote-service connections (SMB/445, RDP/3389, WinRM/5985) to two or more distinct internal peers, deviating from the host's learned peer-connection baseline. A validation XQL confirms the EDR process lineage; a second XQL confirms the NDR long-lived TCP/443 tunnel session in network_story; a correlation rule fuses both ABIOCs with the NDR tunnel session sharing the host's src_ip into one lateral-movement / privilege-escalation incident spanning EDR process lineage and NDR session telemetry — the F2-shaped causality stitch the DC presents as proof Cortex caught a legitimate-tool intrusion no static signature was written for.

campaigns: Muddled Libra operational playbook — hypervisor abuse, lateral tool transfer, and offline DC credential theft (2024-2026)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-EDR-015 — Lateral tool transfer + tunnel + remote-service fan-out for Cortex T1570 ABIOC validation (Muddled Libra playbook, SAFE-MODE markers)

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM agent installed on the target so per-process and network telemetry reaches xdr_data, and NGFW/NDR session telemetry reaches network_story.

A baseline window has elapsed during which the host ran only its normal software and never transferred+executed a fresh tunneler or fanned out remote-service connections, so Cortex learned the endpoint's lateral-movement baseline.

payload.code:
# SAFE-MODE. No real chisel/psexec binaries, no real tunnel, no real peer
# connections. The step writes benign marker files named for the Muddled Libra
# tooling and runs local, loopback-only actions so the lateral-tool-transfer
# process/network shape is observable in xdr_data without any real egress.
set -euo pipefail
HTTPS_HOST="${HTTPS_HOST:-127.0.0.1}"
WORK=/tmp/cortexsim_edr015
mkdir -p "$WORK"
# (1) T1570 archive fetch over HTTPS (loopback; benign marker if unreachable)
curl -s --max-time 5 "https://${HTTPS_HOST}/goon.zip" -o "$WORK/goon.zip" 2>/dev/null || echo 'SAFE-MODE goon.zip marker' > "$WORK/goon.zip"
# (2) write+execute a never-before-seen tunneler marker (chisel)
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho cortexsim-edr015-chisel-tunnel-safe-marker\n' > "$WORK/chisel.exe"
chmod +x "$WORK/chisel.exe"; "$WORK/chisel.exe" || true
# (3) remote-service fan-out marker (psexec) toward loopback peers
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho cortexsim-edr015-psexec-fanout-safe-marker\n' > "$WORK/psexec.exe"
chmod +x "$WORK/psexec.exe"
for peer in 127.0.0.2 127.0.0.3; do "$WORK/psexec.exe" "$peer" || true; done
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-EDR-015 lateral-tool-transfer markers emitted (SAFE-MODE).'

input_variables.name: HTTPS_HOST
input_variables.description: Authorised loopback/lab host the SAFE-MODE HTTPS archive fetch targets.

expected_artifacts.description: A downloader process (curl) that is the direct causality parent of a never-before-seen tunneler binary named chisel.exe.
A long-lived outbound TCP/443 session standing in for the persistent SSH tunnel to attacker infrastructure.
A newly-written tool (psexec.exe) fanning out remote-service connections to two or more distinct internal peers.

iocs.context: chisel.exe — SSH/HTTPS tunneler used to stand up the persistent TCP/443 tunnel (Unit 42 Muddled Libra ops playbook).
psexec.exe — remote execution / lateral movement toward internal peers (Unit 42 Muddled Libra ops playbook).
s3browser-12-6-1.exe — S3 Browser used to exfiltrate PST/data to an attacker-controlled S3 bucket (Unit 42 Muddled Libra ops playbook).
Staging archive pulled from an attacker-controlled AWS S3 bucket; contained Chisel (Unit 42 Muddled Libra ops playbook).

abiocs.name: Lateral Tool Transfer to Never-Before-Seen Tunneler over HTTPS
abiocs.description: An HTTPS downloader process (curl / certutil / powershell / s3browser) is the direct causality parent of a never-before-seen tunneler or remote-exec binary (chisel / psexec) written to disk and executed — the T1570 lateral-tool-transfer signal. Every tool is legitimate/dual-use, so a hash- or string-keyed BIOC is brittle; the ABIOC fires on the download -> first-seen-tool-execution deviation from the host's learned software baseline and anchors it to the downloader causality parent, not to any known-bad indicator. This is the corpus's first T1570 ABIOC.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("chisel.exe", "chisel", "psexec.exe", "psexec")
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("curl.exe", "curl", "certutil.exe", "powershell.exe", "s3browser-12-6-1.exe")
| comp count() as first_seen_tool_execs by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_name
| filter first_seen_tool_execs >= 1
| sort desc first_seen_tool_execs
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_name, first_seen_tool_execs
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned endpoint software/transfer baseline -> HTTPS downloader process (curl/certutil/powershell/s3browser) -> never-before-seen tunneler/remote-exec binary executed as its child, anchored to the downloading causality parent.

abiocs.name: Anomalous Remote-Service Fan-Out from Newly-Written Tool
abiocs.description: A newly-transferred tool (chisel / psexec) opens remote-service connections (SMB/445, RDP/3389, WinRM/5985) to two or more distinct internal peers within a short window — the PsExec/RDP fan-out stage. The ABIOC fires on the peer-diversity deviation from the host's learned peer-connection baseline (a workstation rarely initiates admin-protocol connections to several servers at once) and anchors it to the tool that spawned them, catching remote-service lateral movement that reuses legitimate protocols.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK and event_sub_type = ENUM.NETWORK_CONNECTION
| filter action_remote_port in (445, 3389, 5985)
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("psexec.exe", "psexec", "chisel.exe", "chisel")
| comp count_distinct(action_remote_ip) as peer_targets by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username
| filter peer_targets >= 2
| sort desc peer_targets
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, peer_targets
abiocs.causality_anchor: Never-before-seen tool (from the lateral-tool-transfer ABIOC) -> fan-out of SMB/RDP/WinRM connections to multiple distinct internal peers exceeding the host's learned peer-connection diversity, anchored to the spawning tool.

xql_queries.name: Lateral Tool Transfer Lineage Observable in xdr_data
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("chisel.exe", "chisel", "psexec.exe", "psexec")
| comp count() as tool_execs by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name
| filter tool_execs >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name, tool_execs

xql_queries.name: Long-Lived TCP-443 Tunnel Session Observable in network_story
xql_queries.query:
dataset = network_story
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter dst_port = 443 and protocol = "tcp"
| comp sum(duration) as tunnel_seconds, count() as sessions by src_ip, dst_ip
| filter tunnel_seconds >= 900
| sort desc tunnel_seconds
| fields src_ip, dst_ip, sessions, tunnel_seconds

correlation_rules.name: Muddled Libra Lateral Tool Transfer + Tunnel + PsExec Fan-Out — Cross-Plane Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(Lateral Tool Transfer to Never-Before-Seen Tunneler over HTTPS) AND ABIOC(Anomalous Remote-Service Fan-Out from Newly-Written Tool) fire on the same agent_hostname, and the NDR XQL(Long-Lived TCP-443 Tunnel Session Observable in network_story) shares that host src_ip within a 15-minute window. The three signals stitch into one lateral-movement and privilege-escalation incident_id whose causality chain spans EDR process lineage (HTTPS archive fetch -> never-before-seen chisel.exe execution -> psexec.exe peer fan-out) and NDR session telemetry (the long-lived TCP/443 tunnel) — the Muddled Libra lateral-tool-transfer playbook as a single incident rather than three unlinked alerts.

threat_scenarios.name: Lateral Tool Transfer + Remote-Service Fan-Out Detection via Cortex ABIOC
threat_scenarios.description: Cortex's auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOCs learn an endpoint's software-transfer and peer-connection baseline and detect the Muddled Libra lateral-tool-transfer playbook — an HTTPS-fetched archive spawning a never-before-seen tunneler, a long-lived TCP/443 tunnel, and PsExec/RDP fan-out to internal peers — anchored to its causality chain, where every tool is a legitimate dual-use utility no static signature was written for.

threat_steps.objective: The lateral-tool-transfer ABIOC fires when an HTTPS downloader is the causality parent of a never-before-seen tunneler/remote-exec binary.
preconditions: EDR target with the Cortex agent installed.
Baseline window elapsed with no prior tool-transfer of a fresh tunneler.
steps: Fetch the staging archive over HTTPS.
Write and execute the chisel tunneler marker under the downloader.
Observe ABIOC 'Lateral Tool Transfer to Never-Before-Seen Tunneler over HTTPS' fire.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Lateral Tool Transfer to Never-Before-Seen Tunneler over HTTPS` fires within the MTTD budget.
Validation XQL `Lateral Tool Transfer Lineage Observable in xdr_data` returns >= 1 row.

threat_steps.objective: The remote-service fan-out ABIOC fires when the newly-written tool connects to two or more distinct internal peers over SMB/RDP/WinRM.
preconditions: The lateral-tool-transfer step (TC-EDR-015A) has run on the same host.
steps: Drive the psexec marker toward two or more loopback/lab peers on 445/3389/5985.
Observe ABIOC 'Anomalous Remote-Service Fan-Out from Newly-Written Tool' fire.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Anomalous Remote-Service Fan-Out from Newly-Written Tool` fires when peer_targets >= 2.

threat_steps.objective: The correlation rule stitches both ABIOCs with the NDR TCP/443 tunnel session into one cross-plane incident.
preconditions: Both ABIOCs (TC-EDR-015A, TC-EDR-015B) have fired on the same host.
NDR/NGFW session telemetry is ingested into network_story.
steps: Allow the XSIAM correlation engine to converge.
Confirm one incident_id whose causality chain spans EDR process lineage and NDR session telemetry.
success_criteria: Correlation CR-EDR-0015 raises exactly one lateral-movement incident.
The stitched incident's causality chain includes both the EDR tool-transfer lineage and the NDR TCP/443 tunnel session (spans >= 2 planes).

preventive_controls: Application allow-listing (WDAC / Cortex XDR restriction profiles) so never-before-seen tunnelers and remote-exec utilities cannot execute even when downloaded.
Egress filtering that inspects TLS on TCP/443 and blocks long-lived non-web tunnels to unclassified destinations; alert on multi-hour 443 sessions.

Restrict lateral admin protocols (SMB/445, RDP/3389, WinRM/5985) between workstations and to servers via host firewall and tiered administration; require phishing-resistant MFA on the interactive access paths Muddled Libra abuses.
Protect the virtualization layer: alert on rogue VM creation, restrict who can power down or snapshot domain controllers, and encrypt VMDK-resident NTDS.dit at rest.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs against the learned per-endpoint tool-transfer and peer-connection baseline rather than hand-authoring hash/string BIOCs for individual dual-use tools.
Alert on a downloader process (curl/certutil/powershell/browser) being the causality parent of a first-seen tunneler or remote-exec binary.
Alert on a single host fanning out SMB/RDP/WinRM connections to multiple distinct internal peers within a short window.

Stitch the EDR tool-transfer lineage with the NDR long-lived TCP/443 tunnel session on shared host identity into one incident so the tunnel and the fan-out are not triaged as separate low-severity alerts.
